title: The Included Mileage Allowance and Miles Driven Beyond It
content:
A rate class with unlimited mileage grants no allowance and charges for no mile however far the vehicle is
driven. Every other class among the Car Rental Rate Classes grants its included miles for each booked rental
day at collection, in one grant covering the whole rental rather than day by day. The allowance granted is
the class's included miles for each rental day, multiplied by the rental days booked.

## What the renter must state

The renter states in this conversation the odometer reading shown when they handed the vehicle back. That
reading comes from the renter and stands on their word; the allowance itself and the reading recorded at
collection are matters of record.

## Taking the miles off

At return the miles actually driven are taken off the allowance in one movement, measured by the difference
between the odometer readings recorded at collection and at return.

Miles driven beyond the allowance are charged at the class's excess rate per mile, rounded to the whole
mile, and a rental that returns under its allowance is refunded nothing for the miles unused.

## Extending the rental

Where the rental is extended, the allowance grows by the class's included miles for each additional day,
granted at the moment the extension is agreed.

## Where no reading is given

A vehicle returned without an odometer reading is charged excess mileage on the supplier's own measurement,
and the renter may dispute it through a review rather than at the counter.

## An allowance worked through

For a hypothetical hire of three rental days on a class including 200 miles a day, the allowance granted at
collection is 600 miles in one movement. If the odometer readings show 742 miles driven, the excess is 142
whole miles and each of them is charged at the class's excess rate. If they show 540 miles driven, the hire
is 60 miles under its allowance and nothing is refunded for them.
